title: Portable MRI Vans for Alzheimer's Drug Safety Monitoring
one_liner: A mobile low-field MRI service that scans anti-amyloid patients at home or in memory-care communities for brain-swelling safety checks.
customer: Memory clinics, neurology practices and infusion centers running anti-amyloid therapy, plus health systems. Later, manufacturer patient-support programs and payers.
problem: Anti-amyloid drugs require serial MRI safety monitoring for ARIA (brain swelling or bleeding). Scheduling MRI slots is a hidden throttle, and frail 80-year-olds struggle with hospital scanner visits. With blood tests and at-home dosing widening the funnel, monitoring capacity is the next bottleneck.
solution: A tech plus a portable FDA-cleared low-field scanner (Hyperfine Swoop class) in a van or cart, with teleradiology reads scheduled around dosing. Start with a concordance study against 3T for ARIA-E and ARIA-H (early reports suggest low-field can flag such changes, but it needs validation), then contract per scan to clinics.
why_now: Leqembi Q1 sales rose 74% to $168M, with Eisai and Biogen expecting over $1B this year, a subcutaneous at-home starting dose is now cleared, and two blood tests are cleared. Portable MRI and AI reconstruction have matured.
revenue_model: Per-scan fee of about $250-450 paid by clinics or manufacturer support programs, a per-patient monitoring program subscription, and data licensing for post-marketing studies.
non_obvious_insight: The market talks about drug and diagnosis, but scan capacity and patient logistics decide throughput. The regulatory and reimbursement path is uncertain, so the study itself is the first product and creates the evidence moat.
first_30_days: Contact five memory clinics with anti-amyloid volume, lease a portable scanner, design a 40-patient concordance study with an IRB and neuroradiologists, and ask the drug makers' patient-support programs for pilot funding.

title: Pre-Inspected Wildfire Books From Moratorium Zip Codes
one_liner: Turn California's public nonrenewal-moratorium ZIP lists into a supply of mitigation-verified risks, sold to carriers and MGAs who want good business and to commercial-residential owners who need it.
customer: Two payers. Admitted and E&S carriers or MGAs pay $75-150 per bound policy for a pre-inspected, standardized risk file. HOAs, apartment owners, senior-living operators and nonprofits pay $300-1,500 per building for verified defensible-space and hardening reports.
problem: California's wildfire nonrenewal moratoria last one year from the emergency declaration (up to 24 months for total losses), then the protection ends. More than 147,000 policyholders sit in 29 Gifford Fire ZIP codes, and over 64,000 in 22 Gann Fire ZIP codes. Since SB 547 took effect on 2026-01-01, commercial residential owners are covered for the first time, so they will face renewal shock too. Carriers lack standardized ground-truth mitigation evidence, and owners have no cheap way to produce it.
solution: A mitigation-verification package aligned to the state's Safer from Wildfires discount framework. It covers ember-resistant vents, Zone 0 clearance, roof class, and geotagged photo evidence with an inspector attestation. The result is a portable underwriting file. We start with commercial residential buildings, where one manager decision covers many units and the owners are reachable, and then sell the file to carriers as a pre-underwritten book.
why_now: The Gifford Fire moratorium (emergency declared 2025-12-23) expires around 2026-12-23, about 86 days from today. The Gann Fire moratorium began 2026-08-06. The FAIR Plan hit 696,562 policies and $768B of exposure in June 2026, up 157% and 250% since September 2022. Carriers have been restricting writing statewide, and the state has told them to give wildfire safety discounts.
revenue_model: Inspection fees from commercial-residential owners ($300-1,500 per building), plus per-bind fees or a basis-point share of premium from carriers and MGAs taking the verified files. Later upsell of reinspection subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: The moratorium notices are effectively a public, geocoded list of about 210,000 policyholders whose insurability will be decided by mitigation evidence within months. See https://www.insurance.ca.gov/0400-news/0100-press-releases/2025/release002-2026.cfm (Gifford: 147,000+ policyholders, 29 ZIPs, one year from 2025-12-23, up to 24 months for total loss, SB 547 extends to businesses, associations, affordable housing, senior facilities and nonprofits) and https://www.insurance.ca.gov/0400-news/0100-press-releases/2026/release027-2026.cfm (Gann: 64,000+, 22 ZIPs). FAIR Plan growth is at https://www.cfpnet.com/key-statistics-data/. Cotality found 2.5M US properties with $1.4T wildfire exposure (https://www.cotality.com/press-releases/over-2-5m-u-s-properties-face-wildfire-risk-with-1-4tn-exposed). I could not confirm carrier re-entry commitments in this session, so the carrier-side demand is a hypothesis to test with 3 MGAs before scaling. The wedge sells to reachable commercial-residential owners first, and the carrier data sale follows once the files exist.
first_30_days: Download the ZIP lists for Gifford and Gann and geocode commercial-residential buildings (HOAs, apartments, senior living) from county parcel and permit data. Train 2 inspectors on a one-page checklist based on the state discount framework. Cold-call 40 property managers in the Gifford ZIPs before 2026-12-23 and offer a discounted first inspection. Show 3 MGAs sample files and ask what fields they would pay for.

title: Gauntlet Rehearsal Range for Drone Startups
one_liner: A private test range that reproduces the Drone Dominance Gauntlet scoring so new entrants can rehearse, fail cheaply and qualify before the real event.
customer: Drone makers preparing for Gauntlet 2.5, 3 and 4, from Series A startups to hardware teams entering defense for the first time.
problem: In Gauntlet 1 only 24% of drones reached 10 km, and even in Gauntlet 2 only 11 platforms hit 15 km. Each event has a limited slot count, roughly 6 months apart. New entrants burn scarce runs discovering avoidable failures, and few have range access or scoring instrumentation.
solution: Lease land and airspace near a Front Range site and instrument it to the published Gauntlet metrics (range, sortie count, jamming, payload, ease of operation). Sell run-blocks with independent data logs, a failure-mode report and a readiness score.
why_now: About 60,000 drones will be ordered from winners, and the 200,000-unit target by 2027 pulls in dozens of new entrants. The Gauntlet cadence is public, and a wave of Gauntlet 2.5 bomber-drone entrants is forming now.
revenue_model: $8-25K per run-block, $60-120K seasonal packages, and a sponsor arrangement with primes or investors who want pre-screened suppliers.
non_obvious_insight: When a market runs on tournaments, the money goes to the rehearsal facility that every contestant needs. This is the pick-and-shovel of a public competition schedule.
first_30_days: Publish the Gauntlet 2 metrics as a public scorecard and lease a private test site with a landowner. Buy a few reference drones and a logging stack. Sell 3 startups a pre-Gauntlet 2.5 block.

title: Fire-Loss Data Co-op and Parametric MRF Cover
one_liner: Pool waste-facility fire data to price the unpriced battery-fire risk, then offer verified premium credits and fast-paying parametric cover.
customer: MRFs, transfer stations, scrap yards and e-scrap recyclers (pay verification and premium), with specialty brokers, MGAs and reinsurers buying the data.
problem: August 2026 saw 49 facility fires (tied for the 10-year August high), 293 year to date, and 74 catastrophic (over $400K) versus 71 in all of 2024. Public counts cover only two-alarm-plus events, and actual totals may be about 6x higher. Severe incidents average about $1.5M and no one has decided who pays.
solution: Step 1 is a fire-risk score and controls-verification certificate (thermal cameras, suppression, inbound inspection, tip-floor separation). Step 2 is an anonymized incident and thermal-alert data co-op. Step 3 is an MGA arrangement with a fronting carrier offering premium credits for verified controls and a parametric top-up that pays a fixed amount when a verified thermal event crosses a threshold, for fast cleanup and business-interruption cash.
why_now: Losses are concentrating and rising, states are still arguing about liability, and BRACE Act storage-permit debates put battery handling in the spotlight. The expected next step is insurers repricing, adding exclusions or demanding sensors, so verified data becomes the currency.
revenue_model: $2-5K per site per year for verification, a 10-15% MGA commission on placed premium, and data licensing to insurers and reinsurers.
non_obvious_insight: The unpriced risk here is data, not fire physics. The industry's own public numbers understate reality by roughly 6x, so the first party with a real loss dataset sets the price.
first_30_days: Compile a scrubbed fire dataset from trackers, news, fire-department reports and OSHA logs and derive loss-cost bands. Interview 5 specialty brokers. Recruit 5 facilities for a pilot with an off-the-shelf thermal camera package. Open talks with a fronting carrier.

title: Twelve-Week Friend Pods, Paid by Cafes
one_liner: Fixed cohorts of six adults meet weekly at the same cafe for 12 weeks, backed by a refundable attendance deposit, with the venue paying for guaranteed slow-hour covers.
customer: Two payers. Adults 25-45 who moved cities or lost their friend group ($75 refundable deposit plus about $25 a month). Independent cafes, bars and climbing gyms paying roughly $8-12 per seat-night for guaranteed off-peak traffic.
problem: Friend-making products optimize the first meeting, and one-off stranger dinners rarely convert. Research on friendship formation (Hall, 2018) puts casual friendship at roughly 50 hours together and real friendship at about 90. Meanwhile 24% of US adults with only a high-school education report zero close friends (up from 3% in 1990). Every app's economics reward churn, not durable friendship.
solution: Pods of 6 matched by neighborhood and schedule, not personality. 12 weekly 2.5-hour sessions at one partner venue, with a trained host for the first four weeks who then fades out. The deposit is refunded per session attended. After week 12 the pod 'graduates' into a standing-table subscription. Hosts earn a bonus tied to the share of pod members still meeting at week 20.
why_now: Bumble cut 30% of staff (Jun 2025) and relaunched BFF around groups (Sep 2025), which shows demand for friend-making but not retention. Run clubs proved people pay for recurring in-person belonging. Independent venues face weak weekday traffic and want guaranteed covers.
revenue_model: Membership of about $25 a month per member, forfeited deposits (typically 10-15%), and a per-seat-night fee from venues. Host bonuses are the main cost. Scales city by city with a lean local ops lead.
non_obvious_insight: Friendship is a dose problem, not a matching problem. Every product is paid at the moment of the first meeting, so all of them optimize matches. The only metric worth charging on is hours-together at week 20. Venues, not users, are the natural payer for attendance, because a seated pod is guaranteed revenue on a dead Tuesday.
first_30_days: Pick one neighborhood. Sign 6 cafes with dead Tuesday-Thursday slots on a flat per-seat guarantee. Recruit 4 pods (24 people) through local run-club and Instagram audiences and collect the $75 deposits up front (about $1,800 of first cash). Hire 2 part-time hosts and start week 1 in month 2. Track attendance at weeks 6 and 12.

title: Medicaid Hours Wallet for Gig Workers
one_liner: A phone-based monthly proof-of-work ledger that turns gig, cash and self-employment activity into state-accepted documentation and 30-day cure packets, paid for by the Medicaid plans and health centers that lose revenue when members drop.
customer: Medicaid managed care organizations with expansion-adult lines, and FQHC and community health center networks. Medicaid is 43-50% of health center revenue, and an MCO is paid capitation per member-month. End users are expansion adults aged 19-64 with irregular income. The MCO or health center pays per retained member; the enrollee pays nothing.
problem: CMS's interim final rule (June 3, 2026) requires states to implement 80 hours a month of work or activity, or $580 a month in income, by Jan 1, 2027. Compliance is checked at application and at renewal, and a noncompliance notice gives 30 calendar days to cure. CBO projects about 4.8M coverage losses from work requirements, largely from reporting complexity. About 9 in 10 affected patients are expected to qualify for an exemption or already comply, yet many will still lose coverage on documentation. Nebraska went live May 1, 2026 with self-attestation, but about 28,000 people there must document twice a year and the state plans to move to verification.
solution: An enrollee-side SMS and app tool. It ingests bank and payment-app statements, gig platform earnings exports (Uber, DoorDash, Cash App, Venmo), pay stub photos and logged volunteer or class hours. It computes whether each month clears $580 or 80 hours and generates the state-specific verification packet. It sends look-back-month reminders and prepares the 30-day cure response. It flags likely exemption candidates, such as medically frail members, from plan claims data. The plan or clinic dashboard shows at-risk members and cure success. The tool only assists and never determines compliance, which is what federal rules allow plans to do.
why_now: The interim final rule was published June 3, 2026, and the national start date is Jan 1, 2027. Nebraska's live rollout is the preview of what other states will face when verification replaces self-attestation. CMS is encouraging automation, but states are spending on caseworker portals, notices and screening tools, not on income documentation for gig workers.
revenue_model: $3-8 per at-risk member per month billed to the MCO, or a success fee of $50-150 per member retained through renewal. FQHC SaaS at $2-5k per month per site with an outcomes dashboard. Later, state contracts for a self-employed and gig documentation module.
non_obvious_insight: Vendors such as Salesforce are building state-facing portals for applicants and caseworkers. The parties with a P&L at stake, the MCOs and health centers, are not yet being sold a member-side tool. KFF's roundup of state outreach plans covers notices, websites and screening tools but does not describe how self-employed or irregular income will be documented (https://www.kff.org/medicaid/medicaid-work-requirements-federal-outreach-requirements-and-state-plans/). State wage-data matching misses 1099, cash and gig work by design. Georgetown's CCF warns that 'verification in this context means burdensome documentation requirements for enrollees' (https://ccf.georgetown.edu/2026/05/11/the-new-medicaid-work-reporting-requirements-are-here-dont-let-the-nebraska-soft-start-fool-you/). The retention math is lopsided: a plan or clinic can pay a few dollars a month per member to protect several hundred dollars of monthly revenue. Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/03/2026-11094/medicaid-program-community-engagement-requirement-for-certain-individuals and https://www.pointcare.com/blog/how-to-prevent-medicaid-coverage-gaps-in-2026
first_30_days: Build the Nebraska flow first, since it is already live. Recruit 50 gig and self-employed Medicaid enrollees through one FQHC partner. Measure how many can produce a compliant $580 or 80-hour packet within 30 days. Take those results to two MCO member-engagement and quality leads for a paid pilot. Sign an LOI with one health center network before Jan 1, 2027.

title: Condition-Based Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning Sensors
one_liner: Duct-mounted grease-film sensor pods, sold through hood-cleaning contractors, that predict when a restaurant's exhaust system actually needs cleaning and prove the cleaning was done.
customer: Independent commercial kitchen exhaust cleaning contractors (5-50 technicians) as the channel and first payer. End users are restaurants, hotels, hospital and campus kitchens, and ghost-kitchen operators, with commercial property insurers as a downstream discount payer.
problem: NFPA 96 sets calendar cleaning intervals from monthly to annual by cooking type, but real grease buildup varies enormously by menu (wok, charbroil and fryer kitchens versus sandwich shops). The result is over-cleaning in some places and dangerous under-cleaning in others. Restaurants can't see inside their ducts, so they can't verify that hard-to-reach plenum and duct runs were really cleaned. Grease is a leading cause of restaurant fires and property insurers increasingly want documentation.
solution: A retrofit pod at the hood plenum and an access panel, with temperature, airflow or differential-pressure, fan-current and a capacitive grease-film sensor. It uses BLE or LoRa to a small gateway. An edge model outputs 'days to cleaning threshold' and schedules the contractor. After each cleaning the pod records a post-clean baseline, which becomes tamper-evident proof for the restaurant, the fire inspector and the insurer. Start with sensors outside the duct interior (plenum, access panel) to avoid grease and heat survivability problems.
why_now: Cheap MEMS and capacitive sensing plus LoRa/BLE make a sub-USD-100 pod feasible. Documentation expectations in recent NFPA 96 editions and commercial property insurance hardening push restaurants toward provable maintenance. Contractors face thin margins and want stickier recurring contracts.
revenue_model: Hardware at USD 180-350 per hood, or leased. Subscription of USD 25-45 per month per hood, with a 30% revenue share to the contractor who resells and installs. Pilot insurer premium-credit program. Contractor-side scheduling and route-optimization software as an upsell.
non_obvious_insight: The real buyer is the cleaner, not the restaurant. Monitoring turns a commodity route-calendar service into a data-backed recurring contract and cuts wasted truck rolls. The most valuable reading is not the continuous alert but the after-clean baseline, because the actual pain is 'did they really clean the duct?' That is a trust problem no one solves today.
first_30_days: Prototype a pod from off-the-shelf sensors. Recruit three cleaning contractors through the International Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning Association network and offer free pods on 10 hoods each. Log grease-accumulation curves by cuisine type for 60-90 days. Show the contractors their own before/after evidence, then sell the first paid subscriptions with revenue share.

title: Broker Spread Reveal: Two-Sided Freight Ledger
one_liner: Match what shippers paid brokers against what carriers were actually paid, so every broker's true margin by lane becomes visible for the first time.
customer: Mid-market shippers with $20M to $300M in annual freight spend, using 2 to 6 brokers with no real audit, including PE-owned manufacturers and distributors. Secondary buyers are owner-operators and small carriers at $19 to $49 a month, and freight-procurement consultancies.
problem: Each side holds half the ledger. The shipper knows what it paid the broker. The carrier knows what the broker paid it, on the rate confirmation in the glovebox. The broker's spread, commonly 10 to 35%, stays invisible. Freight-audit firms check invoices against contract rates but never see the carrier payout. 49 CFR 371.3 already requires brokers to keep records of shipper rate, carrier rate and margin. The 2024 proposal to require electronic records and a 48-hour response had still not been finalized as of 2026 status reports. Individual drivers who ask for the record get ghosted.
solution: Carriers text or email a photo of each rate confirmation to a bot. Claude vision extracts lane, dates, load number, broker and pay. Shippers upload freight invoices or a TMS export. The engine pairs the two by load number, origin and destination, and date, then produces a shipper dashboard: 'You paid $412K, carriers received $331K, effective broker take 19.6%. Broker A averages 12% on Chicago to Atlanta, Broker B 27%.' It also generates ready-to-send 371.3 record requests. Aggregated, anonymized carrier-side data becomes a 'Broker Take Index' by lane, giving shippers a benchmark for re-bidding and giving carriers a list of which brokers keep the most.
why_now: The pending 2024 rulemaking has put broker margin disclosure on every carrier's and shipper's radar. The Montgomery ruling has brokers on the defensive. Soft freight markets in 2025 to 2026 have shippers squeezing logistics spend. Vision-model OCR now makes ratecon parsing nearly free, where it would have needed a data-entry team three years ago.
revenue_model: Shipper SaaS at $1.5k to $6k a month, or 10 to 15% of first-year savings after a re-bid. Owner-operators freemium, with $19 a month for lane-level broker-take data. Anonymized benchmark reports to procurement consultancies and private-equity operating partners.
non_obvious_insight: The freight-audit industry is blind to carrier payout because it is the broker's proprietary secret. Only drivers hold the other half, as ratecon photos on their phones. Individual carriers who invoke 371.3 get ghosted, but a shipper with contractual audit rights gets an answer, and shippers are the ones who can pay. Drivers are free supply, shippers are paying demand, and neither can build this alone. Handle rate-confirmation confidentiality clauses by publishing only anonymized aggregates and letting shippers request records under their own audit rights.
first_30_days: Build a ratecon email and SMS intake bot in about a week. Seed it with 100 owner-operators from OOIDA-style Facebook groups by offering a free 'your rate vs. lane average' check. Collect 2,000 ratecons in the first month. Through freight consultants and PE operating partners, offer 10 mid-size shippers a free one-lane spread report built from their last 12 months of invoices plus the crowd data. Convert the first 2 to 3 to a $2k a month pilot.

title: Agent Purchase Warranty: The Liability Layer
one_liner: Everyone is building payment rails for shopping agents. Nobody owns what happens when an agent buys the wrong thing, so sell the warranty and dispute layer.
customer: Startups building AI procurement and shopping agents for small businesses (office, restaurant and parts supplies), and the merchants those agents buy from. The first buyer is an agent vendor that wants merchants to accept its agent.
problem: Visa, Mastercard, Coinbase, Ripple and Stripe are all in agentic rails, and Visa and Mastercard joined Rain's alliance on 2026-08-18. Chargeback rules assume a human clicked buy. ISO's generative-AI exclusion is spreading across CGL policies, so when an agent orders 40 cases instead of 4, the merchant says it was authorized, the bank agrees, and the insurer excludes it.
solution: A mandate-versus-receipt adjudication API. The user's signed intent mandate (budget, item class, merchant allowlist) is logged. On a dispute, the API compares mandate, cart, receipt and delivery and pays valid claims automatically. The first version is a reserve-backed service warranty capped at $500-$2,000 per order, later fronted by an MGA and carrier. Merchants who accept mandate-logged agent orders get a 'warranted agent' signal that cuts false declines.
why_now: Agentic payments alliances formed in Aug 2026, DoorDash is live on Stripe/Tempo, and AI exclusions are appearing on thousands of CGL policies (Insurance Business, 2026-09-16). Transaction volume is arriving just as coverage disappears.
revenue_model: Per-order warranty fee of about 0.4-1.0% of order value from the agent vendor or user. Merchant-side acceptance fee. Later, MGA commission once a carrier fronts the risk.
non_obvious_insight: Rails are commodity and crowded, but liability allocation is what decides trust, just as Stripe won by absorbing fraud and disputes rather than moving bytes. Insurers exclude 'AI' generically because they have no data. A signed mandate log is exactly the data that lets a small underwriter price a slice they can't.
first_30_days: Pick one SMB-procurement agent vendor. Offer a free mandate-log SDK plus a capped $50k reserve-backed warranty on its first 500 orders, and record dispute types and rates. Use that loss data to sign three similar vendors at about 0.75% per order.

title: Health-Check Weekends Abroad, Vetted by US Doctors
one_liner: Three- to four-day trips to Korean and Japanese comprehensive screening centers, with a US physician who prepares you before, translates results after, and coordinates follow-up back home.
customer: Americans 45-65 who pay cash for screening: self-employed, pre-Medicare early retirees, high-deductible households. The wedge is Korean-American and Japanese-American families who already fly to visit parents and trust the hospitals; the broader market follows.
problem: US preventive imaging and endoscopy are sold a la carte and priced for insurers: one whole-body MRI can cost $2,500, and an MRI plus CT plus endoscopy plus cardiac workup can run to several thousand dollars out of pocket. Korea and Japan built prevention into national habit, with one-day comprehensive packages (imaging, endoscopy, cardiac, labs) that reportedly cost 40-70% less than equivalent US screening, but US patients cannot navigate the language, the choice of package or the follow-up when they return.
solution: A packaged trip: (1) pre-trip telehealth visit with a US physician who picks an evidence-based subset of tests and avoids overkill; (2) land package with hotel, interpreter and escort at a vetted university hospital health-promotion center, results in days; (3) post-trip visit where the physician turns the translated report into a US action plan and books any follow-up at home. Group departures create cohorts and lower unit costs. Pair with the Workup Cover idea for the tail if a finding appears.
why_now: Consumers have shown in 2025-26 that they will pay $800-$2,500 cash for a single scan, and K-culture has made Korea an aspirational destination for Americans. Korean hospitals run international patient centers and take intermediary partners, and international screening packages are now marketed in English. US screening costs, high deductibles and the coming FDA and Medicare changes for blood-based tests are widening the gap.
revenue_model: Package margin of 15-25% (travel margin plus hospital partner commission where legal), $250 per physician consult (pre and post), and group or employer retreat pricing for early-retiree communities and small businesses. Optional membership for annual return trips.
non_obvious_insight: The right pitch is not 'cheap surgery abroad', which has a bad reputation, but 'join a country where prevention is a national habit'. The unclaimed value is not the discount but de-risking the two ends of the trip: choosing tests that matter and handling the follow-up in the US. The diaspora is the natural wedge because trust, language and family visits already exist.
first_30_days: Contact the international health-screening centers of three Seoul hospitals and agree one standard package and one heart-focused package. Recruit a telehealth-licensed US physician for pre- and post-trip visits. Recruit 20 pilot travelers from Korean-American church and community groups and longevity forums, take $500 deposits for a first group departure four to five months out, and get six seats confirmed. Keep marketing to screening and prevention, not diagnosis or cure.

title: Licensed Local-Language Speech Data Exchange
one_liner: Pay radio stations and call centers for rights-cleared audio and resell it to the voice-AI builders who cannot get it anywhere else.
customer: Voice-AI startups and model labs that need low-resource African and Indian language audio; radio stations and telco call centers are the suppliers.
problem: Foreign APIs are unusable for local voice because of latency and jitter. Startups like AethexAI train small models on call-center recordings and radio audio, but rights, cleaning and transcription are ad hoc.
solution: A consented, speaker-anonymised and transcribed archive with clear licences and revenue share for stations. The wedge is 3-5 stations in one language (Hausa, Yoruba or Swahili), with a sample set for a paying pilot.
why_now: 300M-1.7B parameter voice models now work in production, and Intron covers 57 languages. Labs face scrutiny over scraped data, and Sarvam and AethexAI are raising money.
revenue_model: $20-80 per cleaned, licensed hour, with 40-50% shared with the station, plus annual subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume low-resource data is unsellable because the markets are poor. The buyers are well-funded labs, and rights-cleared audio, not raw audio, is the bottleneck.
first_30_days: Sign three stations, digitise about 2,000 hours and clean 200 as a sample. Sell a paid pilot dataset to one voice-AI startup.

title: Notary Network for Human-Verified Hiring
one_liner: Bonded local human witnesses (mostly mobile notaries and loan-signing agents) sit with a job candidate for a phone-free live work sample and sign an attestation the employer can rely on.
customer: Remote-first companies of 20-2,000 people hiring for roles that touch code, money, patient data or production systems (fintech, health-tech, cybersecurity, engineering, back-office BPO), plus staffing and recruiting agencies placing remote workers. The first buyer is a 30-person startup that cannot fly candidates to HQ.
problem: Video interviews are no longer trustworthy evidence of who is doing the work. Real-time face-swaps, proxy test-takers and AI feeding answers are common: a 2026 Greenhouse survey reportedly found 91% of US hiring managers had encountered or suspected AI-generated answers, and Gartner projects that by 2028 one in four candidate profiles will be synthetic. Google and McKinsey reportedly reintroduced in-person verification steps, but a small remote employer cannot fly every finalist in, and detection software is an arms race the defenders keep losing.
solution: A marketplace of vetted, insured, background-checked local witnesses. The candidate meets one at a library room or coworking space. The witness checks government ID in person, hands the candidate a locked-down laptop or a paper packet, and stays through a 60-90 minute live work sample or technical interview run by the employer over the employer's own video call. No phones are allowed in the room. The witness signs a notarial-style attestation (ID match, unbroken presence, session log, photo) that goes into the employer's applicant file. Sold as a $150-250 per-session add-on to the final-round interview. The same primitive later extends to bootcamp and university oral exams, licensing bodies, and witnessed authorship for authors and artists.
why_now: In 2026, deepfake candidates are ranked among the top fraud threats by Experian, and hiring teams are openly adding in-person checks. Meanwhile mortgage volume is still well below its 2021 peak, so tens of thousands of trained loan-signing agents have idle capacity and already know how to verify identity and witness a signature. Remote notarization and gig onboarding tools make a distributed 1099 witness network cheap to stand up.
revenue_model: Employers pay $150-250 per attested session (witness keeps roughly 55%). Subscription tiers for volume hirers ($500-2,000 per month with session credits). Enterprise and staffing-agency contracts with bulk pricing. Later: per-exam fees from education and credentialing bodies.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not better deepfake detection but a cheap, trusted, physical human at a known place, and the law already has an institution for that: the notary. A loan-signing workforce is already trained, insured and idle. The purchase also gets filed under fraud and insider-risk compliance (nation-state fake-IT-worker schemes, SOC 2 evidence) rather than HR, which means bigger budgets and faster approval.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 signing agents in three metros through notary Facebook groups and NotaryCafe-type forums, with a simple 1099 onboarding. Write the session protocol and attestation PDF in a week; run booking and payment with Airtable and Stripe. Cold-email 100 remote-heavy startups and staffing firms with the offer 'we will send a human to sit with your finalist, first 3 sessions at $99'. Aim for 10 paid sessions by day 30. Publish an anonymized case study of the first mismatch or coached-answer catch.

title: Keep-the-Laptop Severance With Certified Data Wipe
one_liner: At layoff time, employers offer departing remote workers the option to keep their own laptop, remotely wiped and reimaged with a certificate of erasure. The service recovers, refurbishes and resells the devices people don't keep.
customer: People Ops, IT and Finance leaders at companies running frequent small layoffs of remote and hybrid staff (roughly 10-500 people per round). They buy per device, often through outplacement firms and layoff counsel. The laid-off worker is the beneficiary.
problem: The 2026 labor market is low-fire, low-hire, so layoffs are frequent and small, and AI is the most-cited reason in Challenger data for five straight months. ITAD firms want pallets, not 40 laptops scattered across 40 homes. Unreturned devices are write-offs and data-exposure risks. Laid-off workers lose their tools just as they must freelance or job-hunt. Candidates are also increasingly expected to own capable hardware and AI tooling.
solution: On notice day the employee picks Keep or Return. Keep: the device is remotely wiped through the employer's MDM, reimaged clean with an open-source starter kit and optional AI-tool credits, and transferred at appraised fair value, which the employer can subsidize to zero (tax treatment confirmed with counsel). Return: prepaid box, chain-of-custody, refurbish and resell. The employer gets an asset-disposal record, a certificate of data erasure, and a reuse and Scope 3 report. Device-offboarding logistics vendors exist, but they sell shipping. None sells a keep-it option priced as severance.
why_now: DRAM prices are up about 400% since 2024, so even 3-year-old laptops carry real resale value. Amazon's January 2026 cut of about 16,000 corporate roles and AI-attributed cuts are normalizing rolling layoffs. Breaches such as the Mercor contractor data leak make loose devices a board-level concern. Employers face growing pressure to show soft-landing and circular-IT practices.
revenue_model: $40-90 per device fee from the employer. Resale margin on returned devices. Upsell of refurbished, warrantied laptop leases to laid-off freelancers. Referral fees from outplacement partners.
non_obvious_insight: The laptop is the one severance item worth much more to the employee than it costs the employer. It also removes the employer's biggest post-layoff liability, the unreturned device. Small, frequent AI-era layoffs create a long tail of single devices that the pallet-based ITAD industry ignores.
first_30_days: Pitch five HR and IT leaders through outplacement firms and employment-law contacts. Build the flow on existing MDM scripts (Jamf, Intune, Kandji) with a partner ITAD firm issuing certificates. Run a free pilot on one 50-person layoff, then charge about $60 per device. Publish the pilot's unreturned-device rate and cost per device as the case study.

title: Recipient-Priced Inboxes for Outbound Agents
one_liner: A gateway that lets busy people set a price to reach them and makes outbound AI agents bid for attention, refunding the bond when the message proves relevant.
customer: Outbound agents (fundraising, PR, recruiting sourcing, partnership and research-interview agents) that decide per message whether a reply is worth $1-$50 and pay a refundable bond. The recipient side is VC partners, journalists, podcast bookers, specialist physicians and procurement heads.
problem: Agents remove the cost of sending, so high-value inboxes are drowning. Generic AI outreach now gets under 1% replies in most B2B segments, and reaching one buyer takes 7+ touches. Filters are an arms race, and recipients earn nothing for their attention.
solution: The recipient sets a price ladder (for example $5 for a read-guarantee, $25 for a reply window) and rules. Unknown senders get an auto-reply, or an HTTP 402 for agents, carrying a payment link. The sender agent estimates expected value from its own conversion data and posts a refundable bond over MPP, x402 or card. With one tap the recipient marks the message relevant, which returns the bond, or irrelevant, which pays the recipient. We take 15-20% of forfeited bonds. Sender reputation lowers prices for good senders and prices out spammers.
why_now: Agentic outbound exploded in 2026, with agents choosing targets and follow-ups on their own and degrading deliverability. Programmatic micropayment rails now make a $2 bond collectible without a human. Recipients are actively looking for ways to filter AI outreach.
revenue_model: 15-20% of forfeited bonds plus a 5% fee on settled reads. Team-inbox and executive-assistant tiers for recipients, and an API plan for senders that want reputation scores.
non_obvious_insight: Pay-to-email has failed for 25 years because humans underprice their own outreach and hate friction. Agents compute expected value per message, so a price signal finally clears the market, and it only works when both sides are software. Letting the recipient earn money flips their incentive from blocking to hosting.
first_30_days: Build a Gmail and Chrome extension with an auto-reply rule and recruit 50 investors, journalists and podcast bookers through founder networks. Recruit 10 outbound-agent tools (fundraising, PR, recruiting) as senders. Settle bonds manually via Stripe at first and measure reply-quality uplift against free outreach. Charge the take rate from month 2.

title: China-Asset Diligence Desk for Pharma BD
one_liner: A bilingual scientist-plus-software sprint that verifies China-sourced drug packages (raw data, GLP and CMC standing, ownership chain) in 72 hours for US buyers.
customer: Pharma BD&L teams, NewCo-building VCs, royalty funds and mid-cap biotechs in-licensing Chinese assets.
problem: About one-third of 2025 licensing spend involved China-sourced drugs (Jefferies) and the pace accelerated in 2026 (Lilly-InnoCare up to $3.35B, Merck-SciBrunch $2.1B). Diligence infrastructure looks thin (inference): data packages are in Chinese formats, raw-data and audit-trail norms differ, and CRO and CDMO GLP or GMP standing is hard to verify. BIOSECURE, enacted Dec 18, 2025, requires OMB to publish the list of biotechnology companies of concern by December 2026 and FAR rules follow, adding an ownership and supply-chain axis.
solution: A fixed-price 'Asset Verification Sprint'. LLM-assisted translation and structured extraction of study reports. Bilingual scientists spot-check raw data and audit trails. Verify CRO and CDMO inspection histories (NMPA, FDA, EMA) and check ownership chains against the BIOSECURE lists. Deliver a Western-format gap analysis for IND-enabling needs (GLP tox acceptability, CMC comparability).
why_now: Deal flow is at record levels, BIOSECURE list publication is due in about three months, and biopharma layoffs (15,000+) free bilingual ex-pharma scientists.
revenue_model: $25-70k per sprint, $150-300k annual retainers for NewCo-builder VCs, and supply-chain mapping as a second product once the BIOSECURE lists land.
non_obvious_insight: The gap is not legal or financial diligence. It is data literacy and tacit standards, for example what counts as GLP-grade raw data, and Western deal associates cannot read the packages. The same team and database serve a second product, supply-chain mapping, when the lists arrive.
first_30_days: Recruit 3-4 bilingual ex-pharma scientists. Price a $20k pilot sprint. Approach 5 NewCo VC platforms and 5 mid-size pharma BD heads. Build a CRO and CDMO inspection database from public regulator records.

title: Rural Vet Call Logs as Outbreak Early Warning
one_liner: Producers call the vet before they call the state. Anonymized weekly counts of abortions, maggot wounds, sudden deaths and respiratory clusters are a leading indicator that traders, insurers and packers will pay for.
customer: Buyers: cattle and feeder analytics desks, market advisory and commodity funds, packer and feedlot risk managers, livestock and dairy insurers or reinsurers, animal health company territory teams, and state animal health boards (contracts or grants). Suppliers are participating rural vets, who get free early regional alerts and a small revenue share.
problem: Official disease data lags by weeks because it waits on lab confirmation, and ranchers hesitate to report to the state because a quarantine costs them money. Screwworm was confirmed in a Texas calf in June 2026 after roughly 60 years without a US case, and H5N1 in dairy cattle was spreading for months before detection in 2024. Cattle futures at record prices with a 70-year low herd move violently on rumor, and nobody has a systematic ground-level feed.
solution: A 30-second end-of-week SMS or one-tap tally where each vet reports counts by syndrome (abortion clusters, navel or wound maggots, sudden deaths, neurological, respiratory, milk drops) and ZIP3 or county. Counts are aggregated with k-anonymity (no client identity, minimum practice thresholds) and compared to seasonal baselines. Outputs are a weekly 'Rural Vet Pulse' regional index, push alerts when a region deviates, and an API for institutional subscribers. Vets get the regional alerts free, which is the give-to-get hook.
why_now: New World screwworm has been confirmed in Texas and New Mexico since June 2026, with the first infested horse reported in September 2026, and movement restrictions plus sterile-fly shortages make the outbreak's trajectory the biggest driver of cattle risk. H5N1 in dairy is ongoing, federal animal health staffing is stretched, and academic syndromic surveillance systems exist in Europe (Netherlands, France, Great Britain) but I found no commercial equivalent built from US rural vet practices.
revenue_model: $2-10K per month per institutional data subscriber (analytics desks, insurers, packers), enterprise API tiers, sponsored regional alerts from animal health companies, state or regional government pilots, and a $100-300 per month revenue share to each contributing practice.
non_obvious_insight: Ranchers under-report to the state because reporting costs them money, but they do not hide problems from their vet because they need the vet's drugs and help. The vet's phone is the earliest sensor in the system, and vets cannot share client data but can share counts. Contrarian point: the absence of calls is also a signal, because call volume drops when producers hide problems during a quarantine.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 large-animal practices in Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Kansas and Nebraska through state VMA lists and large-animal vet Facebook groups. Build the weekly tally as a plain SMS survey, with no software integration. Publish a free regional weekly newsletter to the vets as the hook. Backtest screwworm lead time against USDA confirmation dates and pitch 3 market-advisory or cattle analytics shops for a $1-2K per month paid pilot.

title: Program Survival Analytics for Regional Universities
one_liner: A subscription that tells provosts which degree programs will fail the new federal earnings tests and loan-cap economics as AI hollows out their feeder occupations, with a redesign playbook.
customer: Provosts, institutional research offices and deans at regional universities, master's-heavy colleges and online providers ($20-60k a year), plus state systems.
problem: As I understand the 2025 budget law (verify specifics), programs whose graduates don't out-earn benchmarks can lose loan eligibility, and Grad PLUS ended for new borrowers with new caps from July 2026. Graduate programs in cognitive fields (analytics, MBA, MS CS, communications) rely on borrowing, while entry-level demand is falling (NY Fed: 42% recent-grad underemployment). Institutions see it only when enrollment drops.
solution: A program-level model combining College Scorecard earnings, occupation-level job-posting trends, AI-exposure scores and enrollment and borrowing data. It delivers early-warning flags, a scenario tool, recommended pivots (in-degree apprenticeships, short credentials, employer co-design) backed by real employer demand signals, and board-ready compliance reporting.
why_now: The new loan and accountability rules began July 2026, the AI-driven junior hiring freeze is measurable (Stanford: 19% gap for ages 22-25), and university budgets are tight.
revenue_model: Annual licence of $20-60k, program-redesign consulting and state-system contracts.
non_obvious_insight: Universities already face compliance deadlines, but nobody has tied AI exposure to the earnings-test math. A federal deadline creates budget urgency that 'future of work' advice never gets. The first programs to fail are likely master's degrees in cognitive fields.
first_30_days: Build the model from public Scorecard data for ~200 institutions as a proof. Generate 'programs at risk' reports for 20 target universities' master's programs and email institutional-research directors and provosts. Sell three $7.5k pilot diagnostics.

title: Master-Leased Housing to Recruit Care Workers Domestically
one_liner: Asset-light staff housing near care facilities that lets operators recruit domestic workers from a wider radius, starting with stranded worker apartments.
customer: Nursing homes, assisted-living and memory-care operators (5-40 sites) and home-care agencies in tight labor markets such as Wisconsin and rural areas.
problem: The visa pause cuts off the overseas pipeline. Direct care workers are paid little (66% earn under $35k), so domestic recruits can't afford to relocate to where beds are staffed. Closed beds and wings in Wisconsin show the cost. Turnover of 77-80% means every hire has to be retained.
solution: Master-lease or take over apartments near facilities, furnish them, and sublease bed by bed to employees at below-market rent. Employers fund the gap ($300-600 per bed per month) under a guarantee. Add a 3-month 'landing pad' with transport, CNA certification and ESL classes, and a relocation pipeline from oversupplied labor markets (laid-off retail and hospitality workers).
why_now: Wisconsin nursing homes spent $100k+ on apartments for overseas workers and then abandoned the plan when visa access closed, so there are stranded assets to take over. About 350,000 Haitians lost TPS on Aug 4, and about one in five immigrant direct-care workers come from countries hit by the 75-country visa pause.
revenue_model: Per-bed monthly management margin ($100-200 on top of rent), employer subsidy, and a $1,500 placement fee per hire retained at 90 days.
non_obvious_insight: When foreign labor is cut off, housing rather than wages becomes the binding constraint to domestic recruitment. A 20-bed closed wing loses over $1M a year in revenue, so a $7k a year housing subsidy per worker is trivially worth it.
first_30_days: Approach the Wisconsin operators who bought apartments and offer to operate and re-let them to domestic hires. Run a 12-bed pilot in one town with two operators and track time-to-fill and 90-day retention.

title: Human Bench Network for AI Agents
one_liner: An API-fronted network of laid-off expert bench scientists who run ad hoc wet-lab experiments for AI agents and return machine-readable execution records.
customer: AI-first biotechs, AI-for-science startups and university groups (5-60 people, seed to Series B) that run agent swarms but have no wet lab; later, programs adjacent to frontier labs.
problem: Agent swarms now propose far more experiments than anyone can run. Anthropic's run went from 200,000+ reverse transcriptases to 20 candidates using ~950 agents in 21 hours. Stanford's Virtual Biotech (37,000 agents, Science, Sept 17, 2026) says the next step is testing findings in real labs. Cloud labs and robots handle fixed assays, but not ad hoc molecular biology: Anthropic itself found robotics less conducive to ad hoc workflows and kept human scientists at the bench. Human review and bench work are the bottleneck.
solution: Ticketed experiments through an API or MCP endpoint. The agent proposes a protocol and a senior scientist does feasibility triage. A vetted contractor then runs it at sublet or surplus benches, BSL-1/2 only. Each job returns a signed record that separates AI proposal, human edit and physical execution (deviations, photos, instrument logs, raw data). Fixed price per experiment. Start with commodity molecular biology: cloning, small-scale expression and purification, ELISA/BLI/qPCR, enzyme activity, bacterial and cell-culture assays.
why_now: Frontier labs and Stanford now say publicly that bench execution is the bottleneck. BioSpace tracks 15,000+ biopharma job cuts across 50+ companies in 2026, which supplies skilled hands. The OpenAI Foundation plans to distribute $1B by year-end through Public Data for Health, which creates grant-funded demand for data generation. Lab Manager notes there is no sign-off standard for AI-directed experiments, and this record format supplies one. Anthropic has said it wants to work with other scientists.
revenue_model: $1.5-8k per experiment at roughly 35-45% gross margin, monthly retainers with minimum volumes for agent-heavy customers, and a premium for 48-hour turnaround. The platform keeps a take rate on contractor labor.
non_obvious_insight: Compute is now nearly free compared with bench throughput, and robots failed as the universal answer because real biology is ad hoc. The defensible assets are a pre-vetted pool of humans and a structured execution record that agents can learn from. Humans become the last-mile actuator for AI. Adaptyv and cloud labs cover single fixed assays; nobody sells the long tail of one-off experiments.
first_30_days: Recruit 10-15 laid-off molecular biologists in Boston, SF and San Diego through layoff trackers and alumni groups. Rent 2-3 sublet benches or surplus CRO benches. Define three ticket types with fixed prices. Pitch 10 AI protein-design and agent startups and close 3-5 pilots. Aim for the first 20 paid experiments and publish the sample record schema.

title: Launch-or-Rebook Guarantees for Rocket-Chasing Travelers
one_liner: A 'Launch Flex' add-on that hotels, charters and viewing events sell to fans, promising a rebook credit or refund if the target launch slips or scrubs, priced from launch history and weather.
customer: Space Coast and Starbase-area lodging, boat and viewing charters, ticketed viewing events and tour companies. Fans buy the add-on, and operators keep most of the premium.
problem: With 321 orbital launches in 2025 and Starship reaching orbit on 28 Sep 2026, launch-chasing has become a travel subculture. Dates slip and scrub, rates are non-refundable, and fans hesitate to commit. Operators either eat cancellations or lose bookings, and launch-night price spikes breed disputes.
solution: An embeddable add-on for operators' booking pages ($19-49). If the target launch slips beyond a defined window, the guest gets a rebook credit for the next launch or a partial refund. Risk is priced by vehicle, pad, provider and season from public launch logs and weather, starting as an operator-issued credit and later reinsured by a parametric MGA partner.
why_now: New vehicles and pads (Stoke's $1B raise, Starship orbital operations) add schedule variance and fans. Lead times are shrinking (37.5 to 33 days), and firm launch dates appear only days out. The launch-tourism audience is growing faster than operators' booking tools.
revenue_model: The platform keeps about 30% of the add-on premium, operators pay a $99 monthly widget fee, and later parametric-underwriting margin is added.
non_obvious_insight: A launch is a public, well-logged binary event with years of slip history, which makes travel risk easier to price than weather. Rebook credits let a hotel convert a demand spike into repeat visits instead of refunds.
first_30_days: Build a slip and scrub model from public launch logs. Sign 5 Titusville and Cocoa Beach hotels and 2 charter operators to pilot the add-on on their booking pages, and start collecting fees on the next 10 launches.

title: Silver Crews: Retiree Work Co-ops for US Towns
one_liner: A membership co-op for retirees 62+ that contracts with towns, school districts and HOAs for short, insured, daytime jobs (crossing guards, school and library aides, grounds work, event staffing) and acts as employer of record.
customer: Municipal public-works and parks departments, school districts, libraries, HOAs and property managers who pay per job-hour. Retirees join as members.
problem: Employers with 5-15 hour-a-week daytime needs can't hire for them. Retirees want flexible, meaningful part-time work but distrust app gigs and can't easily get liability and accident cover. A record 4.18M Americans turned 65 in 2025, crossing guards are already the most senior-dominated occupation (nearly 1 in 3 are 65+), and about 15% of retirees say they'd consider returning to paid work.
solution: A county-level 'Silver Crew' modeled on Japan's Silver Human Resource Centers (about 1,300 centers, 700,000+ members). It recruits, background-checks and trains 200-400 members, holds standing contracts, schedules shifts, runs payroll (W-2 or contract), carries pooled workers'-comp/accident insurance, and hosts a monthly social meetup. Customers get a reliable pool without hiring headaches, and members get a community as well as a paycheck.
why_now: Peak 65 will stay elevated through at least 2027, school and municipal labor shortages persist, and municipal budgets favor contracting over adding headcount. Japan's centers have proven the model over decades, while US equivalents are small nonprofit senior-employment programs, not service-contract businesses.
revenue_model: Mark-up of roughly 15-25% on member pay billed to customers, small annual member dues, and margin on pooled insurance.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input isn't retiree labor, it's the wrapper. A town can't onboard a 68-year-old for six hours a week, but a co-op with pooled accident cover, one background-check process and a single invoice can. Japanese centers work because the arrangement is legally a contract for a task, not a job, which strips out friction. The social meetup is the retention engine, and it is what makes seniors choose this over Uber or DoorDash.
first_30_days: Pick one retiree-dense county (Florida, Arizona or a New England town). Sign 3 pilot contracts (an HOA, a school district and a library) using an existing PEO for payroll and workers' comp. Recruit 40 retirees through senior centers, churches and Nextdoor. Run the first paid shifts within 4 weeks and invoice monthly.

title: Grid-Code Commissioning for AI Campuses
one_liner: A test-and-certify service that validates how an AI campus behaves toward the grid (ride-through, load swings, oscillations), produces the field data transmission owners now must demand, and signs off on it.
customer: Owners of 50-500 MW computational-load sites (neoclouds, colo developers, hyperscalers' second-tier builds) that must satisfy a transmission owner's new commissioning process. Secondary: commissioning agents lacking grid-side capability who subcontract the work, and utilities that want a standard test-and-model package to accept.
problem: Traditional commissioning tests the facility against its own failures: pull the utility feed, gensets pick up, resistive load banks hold steady load. It does not test how UPS systems, rectifiers and GPU power supplies respond to voltage sags and frequency dips, or how synchronized training-job power swings interact with the grid. In July 2024 about 1,500 MW of data center load in Virginia dropped off in seconds. NERC's May 2026 Level 3 alert now calls for detailed load modeling, annual stability studies and a commissioning process for computational loads. Transmission owners have nothing to point at, owners have no test protocol, and everyone is using generic vendor models.
solution: A hardware-agnostic test package. Rent existing programmable AI-load emulators (Vertiv, PowerLoad and other liquid-cooled GPU-emulating load banks already exist), add high-speed PMU and power-quality recorders, and run a standard protocol: voltage and frequency ride-through, ramp and step-load profiles from real training traces, oscillation checks, and backup-transfer behavior under dynamic load. Deliver a PE-stamped report and an EMT/PSS/E model-validation dataset shaped for the transmission owner's interconnection group. Offer the same protocol to utilities as a certificate template. The value is the protocol, the sign-off and the model validation, not the hardware.
why_now: NERC issued a Level 3 Alert on May 4, 2026. FERC ordered NERC to file mandatory reliability standards for computational loads by Dec 31, 2026. Texas's SB 6 large-load rule is also expected by year end. The emulator hardware finally exists, but the commissioning process and accepted evidence package do not. The first owners to energize in late 2026 and 2027 will need this or wait months for the utility to sign off.
revenue_model: $150K-400K fixed fee per site (test campaign, report, model validation). $30K-80K per additional hall. Subcontract margin when working under Cx agents. Annual re-test and monitoring subscription of $40K-100K per site. Later, licensing of the protocol to utilities.
non_obvious_insight: Commissioning teams are excellent at proving the facility survives a grid failure and almost blind to proving the grid survives the facility. The IST script stops at the fence line. The utility's planners are working from datasheet models that nobody has ever field-validated, and the person best placed to bridge the two (a data center Cx lead who has run a hundred pull-the-plug tests) has never talked to a transmission planner.
first_30_days: Hire or partner with 2 power-systems engineers (an EMT/protection specialist and a load-bank/field-test lead). Write a public 'reading the NERC Level 3 alert as a commissioning test plan' whitepaper. Pitch 5 commissioning agents on white-label subcontract. Line up an emulator rental partner. Offer a discounted pilot to a 20-50 MW neocloud or colo site heading for energization in the next 6 months, priced at cost in exchange for a published (anonymized) case study and a transmission owner introduction.

title: Shared Apprentice Pools for Office Work
one_liner: A group-training organisation (the Australian trades model) for white-collar work. It employs new grads, trains them to supervise AI output, and rotates them across several mid-size hosts that share the cost and get first pick.
customer: Mid-size (100-2,000 employee) accounting firms, insurance brokerages, property managers, logistics and healthcare-admin employers pay host fees. The new grads are W-2 employees of the pool.
problem: Each employer rationally stops hiring juniors because AI absorbs junior tasks and trained juniors get poached. Collectively that empties the 3-5-year-experience pipeline around 2029. Stanford finds 22-25-year-olds in exposed jobs 19% below trend, and 42% of recent grads are underemployed.
solution: The pool hires 25-40 juniors per cohort and gives 8 weeks of workflow-specific training (AI-assisted bookkeeping, claims triage, contract abstraction). It then places them 2-3 days a week across up to three hosts for $38-50/hr as supervised AI-assist analysts with QA metrics. Senior mentors get stipends, and hosts pay a fixed conversion fee at months 12-18. The pool handles payroll, insurance and HR.
why_now: The freeze is widening (Aug 2026 Stanford revision), and AI tools make a trained junior productive from week two. Employers are stuck in a prisoner's-dilemma on training. Pooled employment is a proven fix in Australian trades and in Germany's dual system.
revenue_model: Host fees at 25-35% gross margin, plus conversion fees of $8-15k per hire.
non_obvious_insight: The junior freeze is a coordination failure (a training externality), not a technology fact. Hosts are buying a cheap call option on the scarce 2029 mid-level hire, and pooling removes the poaching fear that blocks individual employers.
first_30_days: Pick one vertical with retiring owner-operators (independent insurance brokerages or small CPA firms). Sign 6 hosts at a pilot rate through a state society or trade association. Hire 10 grads via college career centres. Use a PEO for payroll so you build no HR infrastructure.

title: Independent-Pricing Ledger for Algorithmic Antitrust Risk
one_liner: A neutral logbook beside revenue-management software that proves humans set rents and room rates independently, and doubles as the underwriting file for algorithmic-collusion defense cover.
customer: Mid-size multifamily operators (2k-25k units), hotel groups and self-storage and student-housing operators using shared-pricing algorithms, plus their antitrust counsel and D&O or defense-cost carriers.
problem: The DOJ's RealPage settlement (Nov 2025) bars use of competitors' nonpublic data and alignment of prices. California and New York banned algorithmic rent-setting in Oct 2025. Class actions continue against landlords, not just vendors. Liability turns on whether users set prices independently or rubber-stamped a pooled tool, and on data provenance. Operators cannot produce that evidence, and carriers will not underwrite defense costs without it.
solution: A light ledger fed by exports or APIs from Yardi, RealPage, Entrata, Duetto and similar tools. It records recommended versus adopted price, override reason codes and data-provenance flags. It produces a quarterly 'independence attestation' reviewed by an outside economist, includes a simulator showing the revenue cost of overriding (often small), and packages an underwriting-grade file for defense-cost cover. Design it under counsel's privilege from day one.
why_now: Enforcement plus new state and city laws hit in late 2025 and 2026, and the settlements set monitoring expectations. Mid-market operators are the next wave of defendants and cannot afford bespoke audits. Insurers are simultaneously narrowing AI and antitrust cover.
revenue_model: $1.50-4 per unit per year (about $6-20k for a 5k-unit operator), $10-25k per year for economist attestation, and 10-15% of the defense-cost premium placed.
non_obvious_insight: The legal variable is not the algorithm's accuracy but its acceptance rate and data provenance, and both are just logs. Evidence must exist before the subpoena arrives. The ledger also becomes the first actuarial dataset for algorithmic-antitrust risk, which no carrier has.
first_30_days: Partner with an ex-DOJ or FTC economist and an antitrust boutique. Build CSV-only ingestion for two property-management systems. Approach 10 mid-size operators through a National Apartment Association state affiliate and their counsel. Sell a $7.5k 'independence audit' of the last 12 months of pricing decisions as the entry product, delivered services-first.
